There are severals but this quest made me cry, no voice acting, no beautiful cinematic, just a note found in a frozen body.

I found with a note, the note is meant for her beloved wife who will be waiting for him, he is sorry he died and could not make it to her he died trying, there is a request in the note, that for whoever finds it to please take it to her so she will know what happened to him, the note also describes the place where she was going to wait for him.

You arrive at the place where they were supposed to be reunited, and you find a frozen body, there is a female in the kneeling position, she waited for him she died there alone and frozen, each one of them loved the other to the point in which they would have done anything for the other, now they are both gone and neither had the chance to say good bye.

When I finished this quest I just stood there for a few minutes contemplating, then another players arrived, a male Orc, we both looked at each other for a few seconds, we both knew what had happened there, I said "Well this is heart breaking", he agreed, he wished me a good journey and safe travels, I did likewise, for a small period of time we were both connected by I like to think that we both were thinking about our loved ones and fragile life is, if you love somebody let them know it, every single day.

I was playing Battlefield: 1943 in dogfight mode, which only allows air combat, going anywhere on the map other than an aircraft carrier without a plane is instant death. At one point, I managed to get behind an enemy plane in an almost perfect position to take him down. There were no threats to me around, and he had nowhere to run. Of course, I opened fire and made pretty quick work of him. At the last second though, he bailed out, opting for the out of bounds suicide for not being in the plane, instead of giving me the points for a kill. One of my stray bullets scored a headshot as he was falling from his plane though, and I destroyed the vehicle. Which means I scored 5 points for destroying an enemy vehicle, 10 points for killing an enemy, and a 5 point headshot bonus. If he stayed in the plane, I'd have gotten 15 points for a vehicle kill.
My memory doesn't go that far back XD While I have plenty of moments that I like, none of them stand out apart from each other.

Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time --- the first 30 seconds of the game when Navi is flying around trying to find Link. This moment is forever ingrained into my brain...Nothing has ever come close to making me feel this 'awestruck' in a game.
Gerudo Valley theme song and crossing the desert did it for me.

Are we talking holy shit that's incredible, or holy shit what the fuck just happened there?

If the latter, the first one to come to mind is FEAR 2. That rape ending...had to sit down for a bit on that one. It didn't quite register in my head what Alma was doing to the protagonist until she shows up preggers.

Oh well I have 2 that happen in a console, and a MMO.

First was probably Chrono Trigger. Yep, well I had two games that I was going to play, first was Final Fantasy 3, which was a bit more known, but unknown to me that I had already decided to play, the 2nd game was Chrono Trigger. I passed it off actually because I had no idea what it was, and I wasn't going to play it first. Fast forward about a month, I've beaten FF3, awesome game. Well then, I guess it's your turn. Oh cool it's an RPG, balloons are popping, I started to explore the fair. Everything is going good, OH MY GOD, WTF, what's going on?! I traveled to a different place? What, wait what? Medieval times! Awesome. WTF a FROG!! This trial is awesome. The... future? It's really bleak. Robo. Then I just came.

That's about how I can describe my experience playing that game and it has since become one of my favorite classic games.

The next experience was with World of Warcraft. I was introduced to it by someone at work. I leveled up a bit with my friends helping me as a Paladin. I explored Elwynn Forest, it was pretty awesome. Then, for some reason, my friends decide to take me to Westfall. To be honest, I had no idea I could go to a different area, it was just mindblowing really. But it didn't end there, after a few more levels, they decide to take me on a journey. Go through the train in Stormwind into another are, Ironforge, they take me out to Loch Modan, through the series of tunnels and passages to get to Wetlands. Into the boat and go to ANOTHER CONTINENT! Pass the Dustwallow Marsh area into The Barrens, and Dinosaurs that were beyond my level at the time. Then we went back and camped at the Shady Inn ruins, and that was our guild name. But it didn't end there, we Hearthstoned back to Stormwind and then to Westfall into my very first instance. The Deadmines, my god, that was just an amazing experience that ended with us camping outside of the exit and watching the virtual moon in the sky before I logged out, unable to sleep.

It was a ride really that lasted until close to the end of Wrath and just before I got a chance to experience Cataclysm, but it was still a very awesome game full of just so many amazing people, and the occasional asshole, some in game romance that was awesome and heartbreaking, guilds being created, disbanded, Raids that we spent months on, cybering (learnt lesson to not ever do that again ever in your life unless you know and have seen the person beforehand, but even then, it's just heartbreaking), just an amazing amazing experience that I would probably not recommend since WoW has since evolved into something else that can't really capture how Vanilla was.

Of course the Oblivion sewers, and leaving the vault in Fallout 3 were pretty big, but Shadow of the Colossus, that one has to take the cake for me.
In The Legend of Zelda: A link to the past, when that girl you just saved suddenly turned into a monster.
Phantasy star 4, the first 'fight' with Zio and the outcome of that. That or getting into SEED's plant at birth valley.
In Final Fantasy VII when you first get out of the forced storyline and get to see how big the world is. I could not believe how big the world was. Holy Shit was exactly what I said.

Out of This World/Another World

So many holy shit moments in this game for the 12 year old me. The art style and opening cinematic were above and beyond anything contemporary games had to offer. So much so that the game is still playable and barely shows its age. I think there is an HD remake out there if anyone wants to experience it. It's avalible on Steam for $9.99

Final Fantasy 7. Probably not my "first holy shit" moment but it's the first thing that comes to mind. I didn't know a whole lot about the game so the first time I got out of Midgar I was like, "Holy shit! There's a whole world!"
Ganondorf turning into Ganon at the end of Ocarina of Time.

Running into my first 40 man raid on WoW 10+ years ago.

"How the fuck are we ever gonna kill THAT!?!?!?"

Final Fantasy VI gave me moments that I'll never forget. I have such good memories of playing that game, even though I was only five or six years old when it first came out.

The opening cinematic just blew me away! I wasn't into RPGs, I was really into sidescrollers as a kid but this game just hooked me. I knew it was something special, and it wasn't until I was much older that I was finally able to articulate what makes the game so great. My favorite video game of all time.

Chrono Trigger - when you're in that snowy, barren wasteland, there's no music playing, just the sound of cold wind - and then you teleport up to the floating islands and Corridors of Time starts playing. I was in awe the first time.

Playing Resident Evil 1 and 2. Those games scared the hell out of me. Those small cut scenes when opening a door and not knowing what will be on the other side. Oh man! I refused to play that game at night when alone.
The ending of Journey blew my mind. Graphics will always improve, controllers will evolve, but Journey's storytelling is timeless. Wish I could forget the whole thing and do it again.
Super Mario 64. I remember when it was released a video game store in the mall had a big screen with one dude playing and about 15 of us kids just watching and thinking "I gotta get this NOW".
Getting a ROM of FF6 to run on my Mac... That opening scene & the walk to Narshe in the opening credits. That will always be one of my favorite gaming moments.

The first time playing WoW back in vanilla, right before TBC came out, I rolled a Dwarf warrior. My buddy wanted to level with me and he rolled a human. Wanting to level with each other, he came on his main to Dun Morogh to help me make it to Elwynn forest. He claimed the Dwarf leveling areas were shit and after leveling many of my future wow characters I found him to be correct. We ran through some at the time really boring scenery, he one shot everything in sight that tried to attack me for a good 10 minutes before we made it to Ironforge. I asked him where on the map was this place we were headed, he pointed it out to me and I got annoyed.. I wasnt super into the game yet and I looked how far we had come and how far we needed to go and kinda just put him on follow. I thought Ironforge was pretty cool, not mind blowing or anything.. at the time I had no idea how much time I would later be spending standing on the bridge pillars in front of the AH, but anyway, we headed to the deeprun tram and waited a minute. Deeprun tram wasn't like it is now where you run in and you're lucky to see one other person using it. It was like a New York subway, everyone waiting around for at the time I had no clue. People killing rats, RPing, horde yelling... my interest was piqued a little more. Finally a subway car showed up with tons more people coming off, and nearly everyone waiting shuffled on. I don't know what it was about that, but that was my holy shit moment. This game has a god damn mass transit system.

When the plate collapsed in FFVII killing Biggs, Jesse, and Wedge.
I was 11 at the time and I had no idea what I was expecting, but it wasn't that.
When you first discovered the flood in the original halo.. It was 3 am and I was to scared to go to sleep until I beat the buggers

Probably the Pokemon Emerald credits. After all the long, hard playing where the only graphics were the overworld and pokemon battles, seeing a cinematic like that after finally being able to relax just blew my mind.

Probably the Pokemon Emerald credits. After all the long, hard playing where the only graphics were the overworld and pokemon battles, seeing a cinematic like that after finally being able to relax just blew my mind.

Ocarina of time: This world! It's so big... and I can interact with all these people, climb all these things. That mountain? I get to go explore it, these plains? I can ride a freaking horse over them!

It was the game of my childhood.

Kerbal Space Program. When you first play, you will blow up about 40 rockets before even getting close to orbit. The first time I landed on the Mun was breathtaking and awesome. And then I realized I didn't have enough fuel to get back, but I still felt the most accomplished in a video game that I ever have.

Medal of Honor: Allied Assault.

The first time on Omaha Beach. The mad sprint across the beach, machine gun fire ripping up and down the shingle, that last charge to the bunker. That sequence was amazing.

I don't remember my first but probably beating Pokemon Sapphire after playing it for ages and having to restart it after my brother made a New Game when I was on the stairs in the Pokemon League about to fight Steven!

Maybe also when I started playing Old School Runescape in about September last year with my mate and we heard the Tutorial Island music once again. That was quite the moment.
Minecraft. First night, not knowing anything about the game. Holy shit i have not been scared like that in a while.
When I first played Pokemon yellow as a kid and my Pokemon started evolving My mind was absolutely blown and destroyed, still remember that moment so clear to this day.

When I finally beat ocarina of time for the first time... It was a game I left behind as a child and came back to as an adult. The feeling that I finally beat something that I played years ago, just gave me an amazing "holy shit I did this" feeling.

Oh and Dark souls just in general is a holy shit moment...
Myst. When I realized that I made the. I was like 4 and I'm pretty sure I wet myself.

First moment? Realizing the randomization in Adventure could end-up with an unbeatable scenario. The biggest? Fighting Boba Fett in Dark Forces. Wierdest? My girlfriend at the time saying she would only buy me the game if it had Christopher Walken in it. The game I wanted was Privateer 2.
When you fight evil Santa in Secret of Mana. It was more a Holy shit. What the hell is that..... Santa?

As a kid there very many "holy shit" moments while playing but I remember the very first game that blew me away emotionally. It was 2 years after we got our first PC, and it was Mafia: The City of Lost Heaven. Had me crying in the end and I don't remember any other games having such an effect on me.
Running across the open levels playing against a bunch of friends in a big lan party in Halo CE. I knew multiplayer gaming would never be the same.

I believe it was the original Tomb Raider where you have to shoot down a T-Rex, I was so afraid of that T-Rex I couldn't get past that part. One day I said, 'No, T-Rex-, you're going to die this time." I ran in there waited for the scary doomed music, stood my ground, and kill the loser with three shots of the shotgun. That was my first 'holy shit' moment, and it was great.
The Boy with the Thorn in His Side (live)- Cover by Jeff Buckley
His cover of "I Know Its Over" is one of my favourites of all time. I think Morrissey was a big fan of Jeff too.
His covers are so deliciously wonderful. Admittedly, it took me a while to warm up to his original songs but now I'm in love with his live songs from Grace
His voice is just so beautiful. His cover of Hallelujah is haunting.
Scott Kelly's view from the ISS.
